text:
mira: ran a short probe comparing our slotting-style windowing vs baseline continuous-batcher across APAC (h100) and EU (a100). quick summary: slotting reduces p95 by ~18% on h100 for bursty traffic but increases mean tokens/sec by ~6 on a100 for steady streams. charts: https://internal.redwood/charts/slotting-probe (private)

devin: nice — what window sizes did you try? and what about max_batch_tokens?

mira: tried windows [3ms, 7ms, 15ms, 30ms], max_batch_tokens {512, 1024, 2048}. p95 wins on h100 at 7ms with max_batch_tokens=1024. on a100 the sweet spot was 15ms + 2048 for throughput.

samir: were these runs with q4_k_mixed quant or FP16? any kernel overrides?

mira: q4_k_mixed for the quant experiments, FP16 baseline. kernel selection: default autotune picked cuBLAS-based matmul on a100, Triton-fused attention kernels on h100. interestingly, forcing the alternative kernel on h100 regressed p95 by ~9%.

kai: can you paste the runner config? curious about coil/backlog settings.

mira: sure, snippet below — this is the job config we used for the slotting runs:

```
# run config
batching:
  mode: slotting
  window_ms: 7
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  fairness: cohort
  cohort_decay_ms: 120000
backend:
  quant: q4_k_mixed
  kernel_policy: auto
  kv_cache: chunked
metrics: [p50,p95,mean_tps,token_cost]
regions: [apac-h100, eu-a100]
```

devin: cohort fairness + decay ms — did you see any long-tail starvation for small tenants?

mira: small tenants (<=5rps) saw a small uptick in latency tail at 30ms windows but not at 7ms. cohort decay=120s prevents permanent tilt. we logged per-tenant histograms.

ops-bot: automated-bench-run #1744209876 finished: runs=48, seed=2026-03-19T08:12Z, aggregated: apac-h100 p95=42ms (slotting 7ms) vs baseline 51ms, eu-a100 p95=88ms (slotting 15ms) vs baseline 103ms. mean tokens/sec: h100 slotting=182k/s, baseline=171k/s; a100 slotting=72k/s, baseline=68k/s.

samir: interesting numbers. how stable were the KV-cache hit ratios? that influences token cost a lot.

mira: KV hit ratio was ~0.63 for APAC (burst profile) and ~0.49 for EU steady. slotting slightly increased reuse due to better micro-batch alignment. token-cost reduction ~4.6% on average.

kai: for next steps i suggest: 1) replicate h100 runs with kernel_policy=force_triton on a smaller sweep to confirm regression, 2) run a 24h mixed-traffic stability test, 3) add a cohort that pins small tenants to a soft-priority slice to avoid tail.

devin: agree. also add an eval-quality check for quantized runs — sometimes q4_k introduces subtle tokenization shifts on long prompts. put regen checks in CI.

mira: yep added to backlog. i'll upload the raw CSVs + plots to the bench bucket and tag you all. quick note: slotting seems promising for APAC h100 for bursty use-cases; less clear win for EU a100 steady throughput.

samir: thanks — can you also include the command lines used for reproducing? helps Ops spin up.

mira: copied here:

```
./bench-run --config configs/slotting-7ms-1024.yaml --model rdx-mosaic-13b-q4_k --region apac-h100 --runs 12
./bench-run --config configs/slotting-15ms-2048.yaml --model rdx-mosaic-13b-q4_k --region eu-a100 --runs 12
```

devin: thanks mira, this is great context. will triage ML-2387 and schedule next sweep. :thumbsup:
